newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi management to resign over payoffs scandal.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi management to resign over payoffs scandal.

text.p: In the latest turn in Japan's financial scandal, Yamaichi Securities Co said on Monday its chairman, president and five vice presidents were expected to resign over the firm's suspected payoffs to a racketeer.
Senior Managing Director Shoji Saotome was likely to replace Chairman Tsugio Yukihira and Senior Managing Director Shohei Nozawa was likely to succeed President Atsuo Miki, a company spokesman said.

Further casualties of the scandal, which has also ensnared giant brokerage Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, is expected to include three senior Yamaichi managing directors and several managing directors.
More than a dozen people, including top executives from Nomura and DKB, have been arrested in the affair and both firms have carried out a sweeping reshuffling of top management.

Yamaichi, the smallest of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, is suspected of making 79 million yen ($686,000) in illegal payoffs to Ryuichi Koike, the "sokaiya" racketeer at the heart of the Nomura-DKB scandal.
In June, Koike was indicted on charges of accepting compensation from Nomura for financial losses, in violation of the Commercial Code.

Sokaiya buy shares in companies and try to extort money from them by threatening to expose dubious business practices. Alternatively, they are sometimes employed by firms to quash questions from legitimate shareholders at annual meetings.
Payoffs to sokaiya have been illegal since 1983, but many companies have found it tough to cut off underworld ties.
Last month, the Finance Ministry imposed on Nomura and Dai-Ichi Kangyo the harshest administrative penalties ever meted out in Japan for violations of securities or banking laws.
The scandal coincides with the start of the so-called "Big Bang" reforms aimed at introducing more competition and global standards into Japan's long-sheltered financial sector.
